title: Floating-point columns do not round-trip exactly
lead: Floating-point columns restore to the same numeric value: new manifests transform them with exact decimal arithmetic on BigInteger instead of double.
findings_note: Obfuscator/ObfuscationEngine.cs ObfuscateFloating/DeobfuscateFloating: (x*Scale+Shift) then (y-Shift)/Scale changes the last digits of G17 output (e.g. 131.60538314346292 -> 131.60538314346289) in scripts/test-local.sh sample output; README does not document floats as approximate and test-local.sh does not compare restored CSVs
boundary: **Not in this slice:** byte-identical text restoration (formatting such as `1.50` or `1,000.5` may be normalized); integer, date, or string transforms; changing how pre-2.2 manifests restore floats.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `ObfuscateFloating`/`DeobfuscateFloating` compute `y = x*Scale + Shift` in `double` and write G17, so `(y-Shift)/Scale` is not the original: `131.60538314346292` comes back as `131.60538314346289`, and small values next to a large shift lose low bits. The README calls obfuscation reversible and `scripts/test-local.sh` never compares restored CSVs, so nothing catches it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Obfuscator/ExactDecimal.cs (new); Obfuscator/ObfuscationEngine.cs; Obfuscator/Models.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; README.md; scripts/test-local.sh.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Obfuscating and deobfuscating a float column containing `131.60538314346292` with a deterministic key returns the same number (fails on main). Random doubles, `0`, `-0`, `5e-324`, `1e-30`, `1e300`, `double.MaxValue`, thousands separators and exponent forms round-trip to the same numeric value across scales and shifts. An edited obfuscated float cell fails without echoing the value. A spec without `FloatScheme` still uses the legacy double path.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add an internal `ExactDecimal` (BigInteger mantissa x 10^exponent) with exact parse of the `NumberStyles.Float | AllowThousands` grammar (no NaN/Infinity, bounded exponent), add/subtract/multiply, exact division, and normalized invariant formatting. Float specs gain `FloatScheme = "exact-decimal/v1"`, `ExactScale` (4 decimals) and `ExactShift` (4 significant digits), null-omitted so old checksums verify; manifest version 2.2. Cells that do not parse exactly take the string path and count as unparsed. Document numeric-value (not text) restoration and the digit-count leak in the README.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx`; `scripts/test-local.sh` exits 0 and its new restored-vs-source comparison passes for both sample CSVs; `slicer check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Pre-2.2 manifests (no `FloatScheme`) must still deobfuscate with the existing double transform.
